subject.title: Node host: no SSH transport support + challenge auth fails behind reverse proxy

question: Should `openclaw node run` gain first-class managed SSH transport using `gateway.remote.*`, or should core keep manual SSH tunnels as the supported node-host path while the direct `wss://` auth/pairing work stays in the remote-node approval issue?
rationale: This changes node-host transport supervision and remote pairing/security semantics, so automation should not choose the trust model without maintainer intent.

options.title: Define managed node-host SSH
options.body: Specify the node-host SSH lifecycle and pairing semantics, then implement the narrow core support with live tunnel and reverse-proxy proof.

options.title: Split auth from transport
options.body: Keep this issue for managed SSH transport only and route direct `wss://` pairing policy to https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/91126.

options.title: Document manual tunnels only
options.body: Decide not to manage node-host SSH in core, update docs/diagnostics to point at manual tunnels, and keep only the remote auth issue open.

recommendation.title: Define managed node-host SSH
recommendation.body: Specify the node-host SSH lifecycle and pairing semantics, then implement the narrow core support with live tunnel and reverse-proxy proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The node-host, gateway-client auth, and SSH transport history routes most strongly through this account.
